summary:
Abuja Federal Capital Territory stands under Nigeria's national framework, and no territorial variation from it was identified in this inventory: the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 and the criminal provisions it reinforces apply in the capital as they do elsewhere, and the national layer is carried by the parent record.

The territory's documented trans-specific killing is that of a 33-year-old transgender TikToker known as Abuja Area Mama. BBC News reported on 9 August 2024 that her beaten and bruised body was found along the Katampe-Mabushi expressway in the Banex/Wuse II area of Abuja on Thursday 8 August 2024, hours after she posted a final video, having previously expressed fear for her life. A police statement described the victim as "a man fully dressed in female clothing with no means of identification". Abuja police chief Benneth Igweh ordered a "thorough and discreet" investigation.

The Dial (Issue 25) reports that six months after the killing, no suspects had been charged despite that promised investigation. The same reporting records a petition of nearly 6,000 signatures demanding her murder be investigated as a hate crime. This is the most recent documented trans-specific killing in this record; no later instance is documented for the territory.

The legal floor her killers faced, as set out in the same reporting, includes the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 reinforcing colonial-era laws criminalising same-sex activity as "carnal knowledge against the order of nature" punishable by up to 14 years' imprisonment, bans on same-sex marriage and civil unions, gay organisations and public LGBTQ+ expression, no legal route to change gender, and cross-dressing bans under Sharia in the north and in the Nigerian military. The BBC article notes that although Nigerian laws guarantee freedom from discrimination, mass arrests and detention of LGBTQ+ people are common, especially in northern states.

UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office travel advice for Nigeria, reported by Sahara Reporters on 19 August 2026, warns LGBT+ travellers of arrest, violence, attacks, blackmail and intimidation. The advisory states same-sex sexual activity is illegal and can attract lengthy prison sentences, that some northern states operating under Sharia law can impose the death penalty, that the law extends to people who help arrange or conduct same-sex marriages and criminalises activities involving gay groups and organisations, and that breaching curfews or movement restrictions could expose travellers to arrest and detention. This advisory is national in scope and carries no Abuja-specific breakdown.
tangentialFactors:
The national pattern of mass arrests at private gatherings and hotels, documented in Delta, Lagos and Gombe states between 2018 and 2023, indicates enforcement risk at social venues; no equivalent Abuja-specific raid appears in this inventory.

'Kito' gangs luring LGBTQ+ Nigerians through dating applications to meetings where they are beaten, filmed and blackmailed under threat of outing are documented nationally (Context, April 2024); a visitor to Abuja using such applications faces the same pattern, in which disclosure is the leverage.

localsOnly:
Abuja residents have no legal route to change gender under Nigerian law, and cross-dressing is banned under Sharia in the northern states and within the Nigerian military, per The Dial's account of the legal framework surrounding the Area Mama case.

Nigeria has no legal protections for LGBTQ+ people, and the police response to the Area Mama killing produced no arrests six months on. Many LGBTQ+ Nigerians fear seeking medical care or reporting crimes to the police because of arrest and 'kito' extortion risk.

Press coverage of high-profile custody decisions has treated placement of gender-nonconforming detainees as an open question, indicating that housing decisions are made case by case rather than by a stated rule; the available accounts do not record the section in which a trans detainee is held.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether any Abuja-specific enforcement operation, raid, or arrest under the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014 has occurred within the Federal Capital Territory is not sourced in this inventory; the documented raids are in other states.

The outcome of the promised "thorough and discreet" investigation into the Area Mama killing beyond the six-month mark reported by The Dial is unresolved in this record; no later status is sourced.

Whether the petition of nearly 6,000 signatures produced any official hate-crime designation or further investigative step is not sourced.

The current status of proposals to criminalise cross-dressing nationally, reported by Reuters in September 2022, is unresolved in this inventory, and no Abuja-specific application is sourced.
